summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, style, or format consistently, or embed domain-specific skills that prompting alone cannot reliably achieve. RAG is the better choice when the goal is injecting fresh or proprietary knowledge that changes frequently, while prompt engineering should always be tried first for its speed and zero training cost. In practice, many production systems combine a lightly fine-tuned model with RAG for knowledge grounding.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output formatting, tone, or structured responses that prompt engineering cannot reliably enforce across inputs.
Use fine-tuning for domain adaptation or specialized tasks (legal, medical, code) where the base model lacks sufficient skill even with good prompts.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the underlying knowledge changes frequently or must be auditable and citable, since retraining is slow and costly.
Fine-tune to reduce latency and token costs by teaching a smaller model to match the behavior of a larger one, avoiding long few-shot prompts.
